blogs.title: When the Chest Tells a Pancreatic Story: Recognizing Pancreatopleural Fistula in Kids
blogs.description: Dive into the clinical mystery of a boy who presented with massive, recurrent right‑sided pleural effusions that were nothing but red‑tinged fluid. This post will unpack why PPF can masquerade as a pulmonary problem, highlight key red flags (blood‑stained pleural fluid, persistent leucocytosis, lack of respiratory symptoms), and discuss the pitfalls that lead clinicians to default to TB or empyema. We’ll examine how a thorough history—including accidental abdominal trauma—and strategic imaging (CT, MRCP, ERCP) can shift the diagnostic focus from lung to pancreas.

blogs.title: Blood‑Stained Pleural Fluid: Tips for a Rapid, Accurate Differential
blogs.description: Pleural fluid that’s dark red or hemorrhagic is not always an empyema. In paediatrics, elevated amylase and lipase levels in the fluid can point toward a pancreatic source. This article will review the fluid analysis spectrum—exudate vs. transudate, ADA, cytology, globulin, and amylase typing—providing a quick guide for emergency and PICU teams to rule out TB, malignancy, Boerhaave’s syndrome, and finally asthma‐rare pancreatic fistula.

blogs.title: From Trauma to Thorax: Pathophysiology of a Pancreatic Leak Crossing the Diaphragm
blogs.description: Trace the anatomical journey of pancreatic enzymes that leak through the retroperitoneal space, then climb the aortic/oesophageal hiatus into the pleural cavity. We’ll explain the role of ductal disruption, pressure dynamics, and diaphragmatic defects, and why posterior pancreatic injuries are more likely to yield pleural effusions. The post will also cover how genetic predisposition (PRSS1, SPINK1) and traumatic causes intersect, giving clinicians a framework for predicting which children are at risk.

blogs.title: Octreotide, TPN, and the Power of Conservative Care: Managing PPF Before the Scope
blogs.description: Conservative management is the first line for paediatric PPF, yet success rates are modest. This blog will detail the rationale behind nil‑per‑oral status, total parenteral nutrition, pancreatic enzyme replacement, and somatostatin analogues. We’ll discuss dosing schedules, monitoring for complications, and when to transition to endoscopic or surgical options, drawing on recent case series to outline realistic timelines and success rates.

blogs.title: Endoscopic Navigational Skills: ERCP in the Pediatric Pancreas
blogs.description: Once medical therapy fails, endoscopic intervention becomes the next step. This post will review ERCP indications in children with PPF, techniques for ductal stenting and balloon dilation, and recent advances in side‑hole stents tailored for the small duct. We’ll compare outcomes and complications between ERCP, surgical resection, and hybrid approaches, helping the reader decide when to reach for the endoscope.

blogs.title: Long‑Term Surveillance After Pancreatopleural Fistula: From Follow‑Up Imaging to Lifestyle Modifications
blogs.description: Even after a successful drainage and closure, patients remain at risk for recurrence or chronic pancreatitis. This article will chart a structured follow‑up plan—repeat MRCP, serum amylase/lipase monitoring, and nutritional counseling. We’ll also address the psychosocial impact of recurrent hospitalizations, the importance of addressing dietary habits, and strategies for preventing future abdominal trauma in an active child.
